name: Valampuranathar Temple, Tiruvalampuram (Melaperumpallam)
deity: Shiva as Valampuranathar (a prithvi lingam of sand), with the goddess Vaduvakirkanni (Swarna Padmambigai)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Melaperumpallam, near Poompuhar at the Kaveri's mouth, honours Shiva as Valampuranathar — worshipped in a prithvi lingam of sand — with the goddess Vaduvakirkanni. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, it is bound to the legend of the sage Herandar, who brought the vanished Kaveri back to earth, and is held the birthplace of Sati.

sections.history: Melaperumpallam, the Tevaram's Tiruvalampuram, lies about 2 km off the Poompuhar branch road, roughly 18 km from Sirkazhi and 20 km from Mayiladuthurai, near the Kaveri's mouth. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, praised in the Tevaram by Gnanasambandar, Tirunavukkarasar (Appar) and Sundarar. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later. (Wikipedia lists Mayiladuthurai district; TN Temples Project and Dinamalar list Nagapattinam.)
sections.architecture: A Dravidian coastal-delta temple, the shrine enshrines Valampuranathar in the sanctum, worshipped in a prithvi lingam made of sand, with the goddess Vaduvakirkanni — also named Swarna Padmambigai, Sankari, Gnana Soundari — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The walled courtyard keeps the form of the Shiva temples of the lower delta near Poompuhar.
sections.legends: The lord is called Valampuranathar because, it is said, the conch here was oriented to the right (valam); the lingam is of sand, a prithvi (earth) lingam. The sage Herandar is remembered here for his part in bringing the Kaveri — which had vanished — back to earth, and his jeeva samadhi is said to be at this temple. The place is also held to be the birthplace of Dakshayani (Sati). The goddess Vaduvakirkanni stands beside the lord.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a coastal village shrine. Pilgrims of the Sirkazhi–Poompuhar coast include Melaperumpallam among their stops.
sections.experience: At Melaperumpallam the pilgrim comes to a shrine of the sand lingam near the Kaveri's mouth. Before Valampuranathar and Vaduvakirkanni, with the sea and the river's end near, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple of the coast, and the memory of the sage who brought the river home.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Melaperumpallam lies about 2 km off the Poompuhar branch road, roughly 18 km from Sirkazhi and 20 km from Mayiladuthurai, near the Kaveri's mouth. Sirkazhi and Mayiladuthurai are the nearest rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
